metric_rationale: This design makes the highest-validity cue (feature 0) discriminate in the opposite direction to the majority of the remaining cues on every trial. Take The Best therefore predicts the option favored by the first discriminating cue, while Tallying predicts the opposite option favored by the lower-cue tally. The metric is the proportion of trials on which a subject follows the first discriminating cue. It uses all 96 trials per subject, keeping per-subject binomial variance small (about p(1-p)/96). Under TTB the score is above 0.5, approaching 1 with stronger beta; under Tallying it is below 0.5 because the top cue is the minority tally cue. The design balances top-cue-favors-A and top-cue-favors-B trials, so the raw proportion is not confounded by position bias. This gives a reliable mean separation with tight between-subject variance at N=25.

The metric contrasts, trial by trial, whether a choice follows the full-tally prediction or the stopping-at-the-first-discriminating-cue prediction. Because feature 0 is tied everywhere, feature 1 is the first discriminating cue for Take The Best. On every non-tied trial in this design, the second cue prediction and the tally prediction point in opposite directions, so tally_score - second_score is positive when choices use lower cues and negative when choices stop at feature 1. Averaging over all 96 trials per subject makes the statistic stable under response noise while preserving the large direction-of-effect gap between Tallying and Take The Best.

This is the observed within-tally-difference split by the first discriminating TTB cue. Feature 0 is tied on every trial, so TTB drops to feature 1 (validity 0.80), which always discriminates. I classify every trial by whether feature 1 favors A or B, and subtract the proportion of A choices in the feature-1-favors-B class from the proportion in the feature-1-favors-A class. The trial set has equal feature-1 direction counts within each tally difference d = A_wins - B_wins, so pure Tallying predicts the same A-choice probability in the two classes and the metric has expectation 0. The advocated TTB/Tallying mixture instead shifts the favored class by q times the near-deterministic TTB preference gap; with q near 0.25 and beta_ttb near 5.25 the expected metric is approximately 0.247. Each subject contributes 48 trials per class, keeping between-subject noise low.

All 32 unique pairs in this design have equal feature-win tallies for A and B, so pure Tallying predicts an A-choice probability of 0.5 on every trial. The TTB mixture violates this only when the first validity-ordered discriminating feature favors one option. The metric classifies each trial by that first discriminator using the validity order 0.92, 0.88, 0.80, 0.72, 0.65, 0.60, 0.55, 0.52, then returns the difference in A-choice rate between first-discriminator-favors-A and first-discriminator-favors-B trials. Pure Tallying gives approximately 0.0, while the mixture gives approximately 0.62 minus 0.38, about 0.25, providing a large and stable contrast.
